definition: Templates are reusable starting points for documents, projects, campaigns, or workflows that teams can adapt instead of building from scratch.
extendedDefinition: Templates package a repeatable structure into a reusable format. They can save setup time and make work more consistent, but their value depends on how closely they match the team's real process and how easy they are to adapt. When evaluating software, look for editable fields, ownership, version history, permissions, and the ability to share or standardize approved templates. A large template gallery is not automatically useful if examples are outdated or cannot be changed. Pilot a template with a real task, measure setup time, and make sure it does not force unnecessary steps into the workflow.
examples: A project manager creates a launch template with owners, milestones, risk checks, and approval steps, then reuses it for each product release.
A sales team standardizes proposal documents with approved pricing language and required legal sections, reducing inconsistent versions.
An agency adapts a client-onboarding template for each new account and removes steps that do not apply instead of following it blindly.
description: Templates provide reusable structures for common work. Learn how to judge template quality, customization, governance, and whether a template genuinely saves time.
